author_reading.rationale: Related flags are independently sampled and then combined by XOR; the observed relation can be torn.

rationale: Independent captures reconverge through XOR after their second stages. Same launch clock does not establish correlation or a required simultaneous observation. Related changes can yield an unintended intermediate XOR, but independent status inputs can legitimately be combined. Correlation and consumer intent are missing. The nine-bit concatenation drops only a leading zero; it does not corrupt the relevant bits. Physical synchronizer implementation and asynchronous reset release/recovery remain external obligations; neither SDC nor sampled digital simulation closes them.

labels.rationale: Independent two-stage captures reconverge in an XOR. SDC establishes a common launch domain, not correlation or atomicity requirements for x and y. Related transitions can produce an unintended XOR value, but independent levels can legitimately have this structure; functional intent is unclosed. The oversized concatenation discards only a leading zero and does not confound this issue.

Both inputs are timed to clk_a and independently synchronized into clk_b, then explicitly reconverge through XOR. This permits observations from different source cycles; whether that violates behavior depends on the missing correlation and consumer contract. The XOR does not itself bypass either second stage. The nine-bit concatenation truncates a leading zero, which does not confound the crossing judgment.
